taxonomy.note: Accepted in the current Kew/POWO Tradescantia backbone; learner retained at species rank.

evidence: Hays — documented wild/observed in the City of Hays, Hays County.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Commelinaceae index includes Tradescantia gigantea.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed Williamson County treatment of Tradescantia gigantea.
target_zone_range.guardrail: PASS uses explicit county-level flora/herbarium or supporting occurrence evidence; no broad ecoregion statement is converted into an unnamed county.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with size and lower-stem hairiness. Giant spiderwort is the robust, usually single-stemmed member of this trio, reaching about 90 cm in the Williamson treatment; the lower stem is essentially glabrous while the upper internodes become finely hairy. Its conspicuous paired leaflike bracts and relatively broad strap-shaped leaves reinforce the ID.
diagnostic_traits: robust perennial, usually 1-stemmed at the base
suberect habit to about 90 cm in the Williamson treatment
lower stems essentially glabrous; upper internodes puberulent to short-pilose
strap-shaped to narrowly lanceolate-linear leaves, to about 39 mm wide in the Williamson treatment
terminal condensed cymes subtended by conspicuous leaflike bracts
sepals with nonglandular pubescence; enlarged/bract-sheath character useful in regional keys

confusers.separator: Much shorter and many-stemmed from ground level, with conspicuous pilose/glandular hairiness; T. gigantea is taller, more robust, and relatively smooth low on the stem.
T. occidentalis has conspicuous long-stalked glandular hairs on the internodes and narrower leaves; T. gigantea is more robust with lower stems nearly glabrous.

installation_guardrail: Strict PASS complete; install under standing blanket approval.
